family_summary: AI-built pages are consistently lean and tidy in semantic structure (minimal DOM, clean h1/h2/h3 hierarchy, descriptive alts, basic metadata, no forms or spacer images), whereas the originals show heavier, flatter and more irregular markup with richer metadata and legacy artifacts.

attributes.summary: AI-built pages mostly use styled anchors for buttons (2 of 3 sites) with one using live pill buttons, while originals are split across live buttons, styled anchors and an image CTA.
Both AI-built and original pages use semantic class names on all observed sites, so there is no difference.
All AI-built pages have a minimal DOM, whereas all originals are heavy, either div-based (3) or plugin-laden (2).
One AI-built page has image links that duplicate the title link, a pattern not recorded on the originals.
AI-built pages render entries as list items or anchor cards, while the originals use article elements.
The one AI-built page has no form elements, whereas its original has forms and inputs.
All AI-built pages use a clean h1, section h2s and h3s hierarchy, whereas all originals have flat or irregular headings, often with an empty h1.
Most AI-built pages (3 of 4) have complete descriptive alts, while the originals mostly have missing or wrong alts (3 of 4); one site in each set has empty alts on editorial images.
The one AI-built page does not use headings for menu labels, whereas its original uses h3 menu labels.
All AI-built pages carry only minimal basic metadata, whereas all originals have rich Open Graph and JSON-LD metadata.
The AI-built page uses plain img elements, whereas its original uses picture and source elements.
AI-built pages most often use a single header, nav and footer (2 of 4), while originals most often use many headers, sections and footers (2 of 4), with other patterns varying on both sides.
One AI-built page includes an off-screen skip link, which is not recorded on the originals.
The AI-built page uses no spacer images, whereas its original uses a transparent spacer image.
